drawings.description: à droite de ce carré, deux petits croquis : une flèche verticale prise dans une lentille (deux arcs), deux fois, le second arc supérieur portant une pointe — vraisemblablement le dessin d'une homotopie entre deux flèches
drawings.notes: Two small sketches: a vertical arrow caught in a lens of two arcs, twice; the upper arc of the second lens ends in a small hook, drawn as an arrowhead. The strokes at the left of the crop (an arrow, the letters b and Y) belong to the square beside it and are not drawn. The sheet is the back of a computer printout (job control listing); its typed text and the printed bands are left out.

drawings.description: à droite, un petit triangle hachuré, chacun des trois côtés marqué « $x_1$ ».
drawings.notes: A small triangle, hatched with oblique strokes parallel to its upper left side; the label x_1 beside each of the three sides. The three sides are drawn between the same three computed vertices (on the page the strokes stop just short of one another at two corners). The label is read x_1 after the transcription; the letter could also be a y. The triple stroke joining X_{n-2} to X_{n-1} lower on the page, named in the same note, is a triple arrow, a relation to be set as text, and is not part of this drawing. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): the labels are x_1: the page works with a simplicial object X, whose 1-simplices x_1 are the sides of the triangle, and no y occurs on it. Not checked by a reader.
